title: Build a binary search tree
summary: Each new value walks down from the root: left if smaller, right if larger.

checkpoints.text: The tree starts empty: `root` points at nothing.
The tree was empty, so the new node, 50, is returned and becomes the root.
From the second value on, every insert starts at the root and walks down with `cur`.
30 is smaller than 50 and 50 has no left child yet, so 30 is linked as its left child.
Inserting 20: it is smaller than 50, but 50 already has a left child. `cur` has to move down before it can link anything.
Inserting 60: it is larger than 50, so the walk goes right this time.
Six values, one rule: everything left of a node is smaller, everything right of it is larger. That rule is what makes this a binary search tree.
Cleaning up: `destroy` deletes both children before the node itself, so no node is deleted while something below it still needs it.
